input: Get a quote for a whole-house water filtration system

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whole-house filtration can mean just sediment pre-filtering, or a full multi-stage system including softening, carbon filtering, UV, and reverse osmosis — the scope drastically changes cost and complexity.
The home's water source (city municipal vs. private well) determines what contaminants need targeting and what type of system is appropriate.
Water filtration systems range from a few hundred to several thousand dollars; knowing a budget ceiling helps narrow which systems and vendors to quote.
Whether the user wants quotes from licensed local plumbers, national retailers, or online-only vendors shapes where to seek quotes and how many to get.
Knowing whether they want in-home assessments, phone/online quotes, or a combination determines the outreach process and timeline.
Whether there is already any filtration or softening equipment installed affects what needs replacing or integrating, changing the scope of the quote.
The user may be optimising for lowest price, most reputable installer, fastest installation, or a specific water quality outcome — this defines what a good quote looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Get a whole-house water filtration quote
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to obtain a price quote for installing a whole-house water filtration system in their home.

questions.title: What is your home's primary water source?
questions.description: Is the home supplied by a municipal/city water line or a private well? This determines the contaminants to filter and the right system type.

questions.title: Which filtration stages or problems do you need addressed?
questions.description: Are you targeting sediment, hard water, chlorine/taste, bacteria, heavy metals, or a combination? This defines the system scope.

questions.title: Do you have any existing filtration or softening equipment installed?
questions.description: Knowing current setup (e.g., a softener already in place) avoids redundant quotes and clarifies what needs to be added or replaced.

questions.title: What is your rough budget ceiling for this system?
questions.description: A budget range (e.g., under $1,000 vs. up to $5,000) helps filter which systems and installers are worth quoting.

questions.title: How many quotes do you want, and from what type of provider?
questions.description: Should quotes come from local licensed plumbers, big-box retailers, specialty water treatment companies, or a mix?

questions.title: Do you prefer in-home assessments or remote/online quotes?
questions.description: In-home visits give more accurate quotes but take more time; online or phone quotes are faster but less precise.

questions.title: What does the ideal outcome of this quote process look like?
questions.description: Is the top priority the lowest price, fastest installation, highest-rated installer, or achieving a specific water quality standard?
